title: Cross-lingual Few-shot Benchmark and Onboarding Protocol
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview
========

Purpose: This page describes the Cross-lingual Few-shot Benchmark and Onboarding Protocol (CLFB-OP). CLFB-OP standardizes how we evaluate, qualify, and promote models for multilingual few-shot use cases across Redwood deployments. The protocol ties together the eval harness, curated prompt sets, quantization sensitivity checks, quality guardrails, and a short regression triage workflow.

Scope
-----
- Applies to all models submitted for hosted or dedicated serving with claims for multilingual few-shot capability (defined here as producing coherent, accurate responses in >= 8 languages with few-shot prompts).
- Includes models in floating, quantized, or distilled variants.
- Does NOT replace domain-specific evaluations (e.g., healthcare PII redaction), which remain separate.

Design principles
-----------------
1. Representative coverage: include typologically diverse languages (e.g., English, Spanish, Portuguese, French, Arabic, Hindi, Bengali, Mandarin Chinese, Russian, German, Japanese).
2. Robustness to prompt context: evaluate variable shot counts (0, 1, 3, 8), prefix length, and prompt noise.
3. Quantization-aware: run baseline and quantized model evaluations to detect degradation modes tied to int8/4-bit transforms.
4. Operationalizable metrics: use a small set of metrics that map to production SLOs and to regression alerting.

Benchmark composition
---------------------
- Prompt sets: 1,200 prompt instances total (150 per language) split evenly across tasks: translation, summarization (short news), question answering (extractive + generative), instruction-following, and slot-filling.
- Shots: each prompt has versions for 0-shot, 1-shot, 3-shot, and 8-shot.
- Noise variants: for 30% of prompts include injected token-level noise (typos, punctuation drops) to test resilience.
- Gold references: for generative tasks we maintain 3 human references where possible; for extractive tasks we store canonical spans.

Evaluation metrics and thresholds
--------------------------------
Table: primary metrics and promotion thresholds (per-language):

- Exact Match (EM) - extractive QA: baseline >= 0.68 (median across languages), delta to production baseline <= -0.05 for promotion; regression alert if drop > 0.08.
- chrF++ - translation: baseline >= 0.42, quantized delta <= -0.06.
- ROUGE-L - summarization: baseline >= 0.48, median >= 0.42.
- Semantic Embedding Cosine (avg) - instruction fidelity: baseline >= 0.85.
- Hallucination Rate (human-annotated sampling) - generative QA: <= 6% absolute.
- Latency p95 (inference at 512 context, single-request path): <= 350ms for hosted small/dedicated medium tiers; label as "performance-warning" if between 350-550ms.

Notes on thresholds:
- Baselines are model-family specific; absolute numbers above represent typical thresholds used for promotion. Each promotion requires comparing candidate to the current production baseline for the model family and customer tier.

Integration with eval harness
----------------------------
- Harness runner: eval-orchestrator (service) executes jobs. Use the eval manifest format under tests/manifests/clfb/*.yaml.
- Job config must include: model_variant, quantization_profile, shot_config, language_set, noise_seed, and sample_seed.
- Output artifacts: token-level traces, model logits (when available), generation samples with metadata, per-language metric CSV, and embedding vectors for sampled outputs. Artifacts are stored in s3://redwood-evals/clfb/YYYY-MM-DD/{job_id}/.

Quantization sensitivity checks
------------------------------
Procedure:
1. Run floating-point (fp16) baseline run with 5k sampled prompts (stratified by language and task).
2. Run quantized variants (int8, int4 where supported) with identical seeds and prompt order.
3. Compute metric deltas per-language and per-task.
4. Flag if more than 2 languages exceed the per-metric quantized delta thresholds (see thresholds above).

Recommended quick checks (fast path, ~30m):
- 300-sample subset across languages/tasks for int8: measure chrF/EM/semantic-cosine.
- Compare hallucination proxies (e.g., answer length divergence, out-of-vocab rate) before human annotation step.

Quality guardrails and automatic fail gates
-----------------------------------------
Automatic fail gates (block promotion):
- Any language with EM drop > 0.10 compared to production baseline for extractive QA.
- Hallucination rate increase > 4 percentage points in sampled generative QA.
- Semantic-cosine drop > 0.07 for instruction tasks.
- Latency p95 regression > 200ms over baseline in same deployment configuration.

Soft warnings (require human review):
- Any metric with degradation in the range of delta between soft and hard thresholds (documented in the threshold table).
- Significant variance across languages (e.g., median passes but 2+ languages fall into fail region).

Promotion and onboarding checklist
--------------------------------
Before a model variant can be promoted to staging or production for multilingual few-shot use cases, complete the following items: 

1. Documentation
   - Confirm model card includes explicit language support & tokenization caveats.
   - Note any known failure modes and domains with high hallucination.
2. Eval runs
   - Complete full CLFB-OP run (all languages, shots, noise variants).
   - Attach eval artifacts with stable job_id in the release ticket.
3. Quantization verification
   - Verify quantization sensitivity checks; include quantization profile used.
4. Guardrail checks
   - Ensure no automatic fail gates triggered. If triggered, attach triage notes and mitigation plan.
5. Evals QA signoff
   - Two reviewers from Applied ML must sign off (names recorded in release ticket).
6. Performance review
   - Confirm latency and memory fall within tier SLA for the intended deployment mode.

Regression triage playbook (short form)
--------------------------------------
When a CLFB-OP job indicates a regression after a promotion or an automated daily job: 

1. Triage (first 30 minutes)
   - Owner: model-onboarding on-call or the authoring team.
   - Re-run failing subset with seeds and collect deterministic artifacts.
   - Check whether regression is present only in quantized variant or across all variants.
2. Narrow (30–120 minutes)
   - Run per-language isolations to identify affected languages or tasks.
   - Compare token-level diffs and attention-cache divergence (if available).
3. Mitigate (same day)
   - If caused by quantization: attempt alternate quant profile or disable quantization for language(s).
   - If caused by prompt-change: revert prompt preprocessing or pin prompt template used in production.
   - If caused by model weights: roll back to prior model-version and open regression incident.
4. Postmortem
   - If regression required rollback, file a short postmortem and add regression ticket to model family triage board.

Operational run cadence and automation
------------------------------------
- Nightly smoke runs: lightweight CLFB-OP subset (200 prompts) across all model families. Alerts on soft warnings via #applied-ml-alerts.
- Weekly full runs: full benchmark for active candidate branches or new model families.
- On-demand: required before any production promotion.
- Automation: evaluate with eval-orchestrator cron jobs; use monitor job config clfb/schedules.yaml and register artifacts with redwood-metrics under metric namespace: rl.clfb.*.

Ownership and escalation
------------------------
- Primary owner: Applied ML — Model Onboarding subteam.
- Secondary owners: Runtime (for latency regressions), Quantization team (for quant-failures), and SRE (for infra-related artifacts).
- Escalation path: If a regression affects >30% of customers or requires rollback, notify Eng SRE and Product Success within 2 hours.

Data and annotation notes
-------------------------
- Human annotation for hallucination and factuality uses a stratified sampling methodology (n=250 per run) and requires two annotator agreement; disagreements escalate to a senior annotator.
- For lower-resource languages where human references are limited, rely on back-translation + embedding similarity as a proxy and mark results as advisory.

CLI and manifest examples (excerpt)
---------------------------------
Example eval manifest: 

---
job_id: clfb-20260203-xyz
model_variant: my-model-v2
quant_profiles: [fp16, int8-profile-a]
languages: [en,es,fr,ar,hi,zh,ru,de,ja,pt]
shots: [0,1,3,8]
noise_seed: 42
sample_seed: 1001
---

Example eval run command:

$ eval-orchestrator submit --manifest tests/manifests/clfb/clfb-20260203-xyz.yaml --output s3://redwood-evals/clfb/2026-02-03/

Appendix: typical artifact layout
--------------------------------
- s3://redwood-evals/clfb/{date}/{job_id}/metrics.csv
- s3://redwood-evals/clfb/{date}/{job_id}/samples.jsonl
- s3://redwood-evals/clfb/{date}/{job_id}/logits/{sample_id}.npy
- redwood-metrics namespace: rl.clfb.{model_family}.{metric}.{language}
